result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain place-value alignment well and give concrete, ranked fixes for mixed columns: put the unit in the header, treat 'Pending' as a missing value or a separate status, and left-align when the column can't be split. B goes further on tabular figures and decimals, naming the CSS property and saying to pad with .00. Its rule of thumb ('Align by what the column is... If one column is trying to be both, split it') is also shorter and easier to remember than A's longer paragraph. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain place-value alignment well and give concrete options for mixed columns. B adds useful touches, such as the 1,250 vs 12.5 example and handling units that vary ("3 days" vs "2 weeks"). A wins because its rule of thumb is shorter and easier to remember ("Align by what the column is… If one column is trying to be both, split it"), it gives the CSS for tabular figures, and its follow-up rules are easy for designers to act on.
